title: What is TypeScript
description: Understand TypeScript and its benefits for React development.

data.text: **TypeScript** is a typed superset of JavaScript developed by Microsoft. It adds optional static typing to JavaScript, catching errors at compile time rather than runtime.

terms.definition: Type checking performed at compile time, before the code runs.
A language that contains all features of another language plus additional features.
The phase where source code is transformed into executable code.
The phase where the compiled code is executed.

data.title: Key Benefits
items: **Catch errors early**: Type checking at compile time prevents runtime errors
**Better IDE support**: Autocomplete, refactoring, and inline documentation
**Self-documenting code**: Types serve as documentation for your code
**Safer refactoring**: The compiler catches breaking changes
**Team collaboration**: Clear contracts between components and modules

data.title: Create React with TypeScript
data.content: Creating a new React TypeScript project
data.code:
npm create vite@latest my-app -- --template react-ts
cd my-app
npm install
npm run dev

data.title: File Extensions
data.text: TypeScript files use `.ts` for regular code and `.tsx` for files containing JSX. React components should use `.tsx`.

data.title: Quick Setup Steps
items: Create a new Vite project with React TypeScript template
Open the project in your IDE
Verify TypeScript is working by checking for .tsx files

data.caption: TypeScript compilation and runtime flow
data.definition:
flowchart TB

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: TypeScript adds static typing to JavaScript
Improves developer experience with better tooling
data.takeaway: TypeScript makes React development safer and more productive.
